fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact exists when personal or tenant scoped data is involved.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.

fields.Recovery strategy: Stabilize dependencies, restore known good state, reconcile data if required, then reintroduce traffic gradually with verification.
fields.Regression protection: Run the deterministic test in CI where possible and schedule production or staging resilience exercises for runtime only conditions.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results, logs or traces, configuration proof, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert on sustained error or saturation thresholds, rapid trend changes, correctness violations and security indicators.
fields.Required observability: Track request rate, errors, duration, saturation, retries, queue depth, dependency health and problem specific counters.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after tests pass and measured production limits are known.
fields.Root cause: Insufficient design constraint, validation, isolation, capacity control or lifecycle management for this failure mode.

fields.Expected likelihood: High under real market use unless explicitly controlled

fields.Negative test: Supply malformed, boundary, duplicate, unauthorized or contradictory conditions relevant to the failure and assert rejection or safe degradation.

fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact exists when personal or tenant scoped data is involved.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The reference architecture contains API gateway, controllers, schemas, clients and is exposed to real users, real data, concurrency, failures and abuse.
fields.Recovery strategy: Stabilize dependencies, restore known good state, reconcile data if required, then reintroduce traffic gradually with verification.
fields.Regression protection: Run the deterministic test in CI where possible and schedule production or staging resilience exercises for runtime only conditions.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results, logs or traces, configuration proof, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert on sustained error or saturation thresholds, rapid trend changes, correctness violations and security indicators.
fields.Required observability: Track request rate, errors, duration, saturation, retries, queue depth, dependency health and problem specific counters.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after tests pass and measured production limits are known.
fields.Root cause: Per parent lazy or repeated child retrieval creates one initial query plus one or more queries for each returned parent.

fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry

fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact exists when personal or tenant scoped data is involved.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.

fields.Recovery strategy: Stabilize dependencies, restore known good state, reconcile data if required, then reintroduce traffic gradually with verification.
fields.Regression protection: Run the deterministic test in CI where possible and schedule production or staging resilience exercises for runtime only conditions.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results, logs or traces, configuration proof, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert on sustained error or saturation thresholds, rapid trend changes, correctness violations and security indicators.
fields.Required observability: Track request rate, errors, duration, saturation, retries, queue depth, dependency health and problem specific counters.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after tests pass and measured production limits are known.

fields.Automated test: Create a deterministic automated regression that forces the named condition and asserts safe behavior.

fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, rising with scale, complexity, age and dependency count
fields.Expected severity: Medium
fields.Failure mechanism: The application performs an unauthorized action, interprets untrusted data as control data, or exposes sensitive information.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Can increase infrastructure, third party, incident, fraud or recovery cost.
fields.Known aliases: IDOR
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Exercise the condition at realistic and beyond expected concurrency or data volume and record the break point.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Contain blast radius, shed or throttle unsafe load, disable the failing path where needed, and preserve data correctness before restoring capacity.
fields.Negative test: Supply malformed, boundary, duplicate, unauthorized or contradictory conditions relevant to the failure and assert rejection or safe degradation.
fields.Performance consequences: Can increase latency, resource use, contention or unnecessary work.
fields.Prevention strategy: Apply deny by default authorization, least privilege, strong authentication, input validation, output encoding, parameterized operations, secret management and dependency controls.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact exists when personal or tenant scoped data is involved.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The reference architecture contains application, API, dependencies and infrastructure and is exposed to real users, real data, concurrency, failures and abuse.
fields.Recovery strategy: Stabilize dependencies, restore known good state, reconcile data if required, then reintroduce traffic gradually with verification.
fields.Regression protection: Run the deterministic test in CI where possible and schedule production or staging resilience exercises for runtime only conditions.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results, logs or traces, configuration proof, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert on sustained error or saturation thresholds, rapid trend changes, correctness violations and security indicators.
fields.Required observability: Track request rate, errors, duration, saturation, retries, queue depth, dependency health and problem specific counters.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after tests pass and measured production limits are known.
fields.Root cause: Trust boundary, input, identity, authorization, secret or dependency controls are insufficient.
fields.Security consequences: May increase attack surface or weaken confidentiality, integrity or availability if the failure crosses a trust boundary.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Use authenticated and unauthenticated abuse cases, cross user and cross tenant attempts, injection payloads and privilege escalation tests.
fields.User visible symptoms: Slow responses, errors, inconsistent results, duplicate actions, inaccessible functionality or exposed information may appear.

fields.Regression protection: Run the deterministic test in CI where possible and schedule production or staging resilience exercises for runtime only conditions.

fields.Expected likelihood: High under real market use unless explicitly controlled
fields.Expected severity: High
fields.Failure mechanism: The affected component enters an unsafe, inconsistent, overloaded or unavailable state and propagates impact to callers or dependent components.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Can increase infrastructure, third party, incident, fraud or recovery cost.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Exercise the condition at realistic and beyond expected concurrency or data volume and record the break point.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Contain blast radius, shed or throttle unsafe load, disable the failing path where needed, and preserve data correctness before restoring capacity.
fields.Negative test: Supply malformed, boundary, duplicate, unauthorized or contradictory conditions relevant to the failure and assert rejection or safe degradation.
fields.Performance consequences: Can increase latency, resource use, contention or unnecessary work.
fields.Prevention strategy: Define explicit limits, safe defaults, isolation, validation, idempotency, capacity margins and architecture specific controls before release.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact exists when personal or tenant scoped data is involved.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The reference architecture contains data pipelines, CDC and analytics and is exposed to real users, real data, concurrency, failures and abuse.
fields.Recovery strategy: Stabilize dependencies, restore known good state, reconcile data if required, then reintroduce traffic gradually with verification.
fields.Regression protection: Run the deterministic test in CI where possible and schedule production or staging resilience exercises for runtime only conditions.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results, logs or traces, configuration proof, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert on sustained error or saturation thresholds, rapid trend changes, correctness violations and security indicators.
fields.Required observability: Track request rate, errors, duration, saturation, retries, queue depth, dependency health and problem specific counters.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after tests pass and measured production limits are known.
fields.Root cause: Insufficient design constraint, validation, isolation, capacity control or lifecycle management for this failure mode.

fields.Performance consequences: Reconciliation, retry or repair work can increase database, queue and integration load.
fields.Prevention strategy: Model financial state with explicit immutable or auditable records, atomic transactions, idempotency, exact decimal arithmetic, ordering guarantees, authorization checks, limit enforcement and independent reconciliation.
fields.Privacy consequences: Financial records and identity data can create privacy impact if exposed or associated with the wrong user.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.

fields.Recovery strategy: Reconstruct financial state from authoritative records, post controlled compensating entries where required, reconcile external systems and obtain financial control approval before resuming normal processing.

fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.

fields.Required observability: Track ledger invariants, balance deltas, transaction states, duplicate references, settlement status, reconciliation breaks, reversals, adjustments and financial control exceptions.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Financial invariants, atomicity, idempotency, precision, ordering, authorization, settlement or reconciliation controls are incomplete or inconsistent.
fields.Security consequences: Attackers may exploit the weakness for unauthorized financial gain, replay, limit bypass, account abuse or transaction manipulation.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt replay, double spend, limit bypass, account substitution, amount manipulation, race conditions and unauthorized financial transitions.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users may observe wrong balances, charges, credits, payouts, statements, limits, prices, settlement status or transaction history.

fields.Data integrity consequences: Ledger, transaction, balance, settlement, accounting or reconciliation records may diverge or become duplicated, missing or inconsistent.
fields.Detectability: Medium. Reconciliation can expose many failures, but silent balance or posting drift may persist until downstream settlement or customer dispute.
fields.Detection strategy: Continuously reconcile balances, postings, settlement, external processor records and customer statements. Track duplicate references, invariant violations, unexplained adjustments and out of balance conditions.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium to High under real transaction volume unless financial invariants, idempotency and reconciliation are explicitly enforced
fields.Expected severity: High, and Critical where customer funds, settlement, regulated capital or material financial reporting are affected
fields.Failure mechanism: The authoritative financial state diverges from the intended economic event, causing an incorrect balance, posting, charge, payout, valuation, settlement or accounting result.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Direct financial loss, incorrect customer funds, chargebacks, restitution, reconciliation cost, penalties and incident cost are possible.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Run concurrent financial operations at realistic and peak volume, including retries and delayed callbacks, and prove balance, limit, ordering and idempotency invariants remain true.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Freeze or isolate the affected transaction path, prevent further financial mutation, preserve the event trail, calculate the authoritative state and route discrepancies to controlled reconciliation.
fields.Negative test: Test zero, negative, maximum, precision boundary, duplicate, stale, unauthorized, expired, reversed, out of order and conflicting financial operations relevant to the risk.
fields.Owner: Financial Systems Engineering and Risk Controls
fields.Performance consequences: Reconciliation, retry or repair work can increase database, queue and integration load.
fields.Prevention strategy: Model financial state with explicit immutable or auditable records, atomic transactions, idempotency, exact decimal arithmetic, ordering guarantees, authorization checks, limit enforcement and independent reconciliation.
fields.Privacy consequences: Financial records and identity data can create privacy impact if exposed or associated with the wrong user.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Banking, payments, and FinTech.
fields.Recovery strategy: Reconstruct financial state from authoritative records, post controlled compensating entries where required, reconcile external systems and obtain financial control approval before resuming normal processing.
fields.Regression protection: Run financial invariant and reconciliation suites in CI, plus scheduled production reconciliation and concurrency exercises for high risk money paths.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert immediately on out of balance conditions, duplicate economic effects, unexplained money creation or loss, settlement mismatch, reconciliation failure and unauthorized financial state change.
fields.Required observability: Track ledger invariants, balance deltas, transaction states, duplicate references, settlement status, reconciliation breaks, reversals, adjustments and financial control exceptions.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Financial invariants, atomicity, idempotency, precision, ordering, authorization, settlement or reconciliation controls are incomplete or inconsistent.
fields.Security consequences: Attackers may exploit the weakness for unauthorized financial gain, replay, limit bypass, account abuse or transaction manipulation.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt replay, double spend, limit bypass, account substitution, amount manipulation, race conditions and unauthorized financial transitions.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users may observe wrong balances, charges, credits, payouts, statements, limits, prices, settlement status or transaction history.

fields.Mitigation strategy: Freeze or isolate the affected transaction path, prevent further financial mutation, preserve the event trail, calculate the authoritative state and route discrepancies to controlled reconciliation.
fields.Negative test: Test zero, negative, maximum, precision boundary, duplicate, stale, unauthorized, expired, reversed, out of order and conflicting financial operations relevant to the risk.
fields.Owner: Financial Systems Engineering and Risk Controls
fields.Performance consequences: Reconciliation, retry or repair work can increase database, queue and integration load.
fields.Prevention strategy: Model financial state with explicit immutable or auditable records, atomic transactions, idempotency, exact decimal arithmetic, ordering guarantees, authorization checks, limit enforcement and independent reconciliation.
fields.Privacy consequences: Financial records and identity data can create privacy impact if exposed or associated with the wrong user.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Banking, payments, and FinTech.
fields.Recovery strategy: Reconstruct financial state from authoritative records, post controlled compensating entries where required, reconcile external systems and obtain financial control approval before resuming normal processing.
fields.Regression protection: Run financial invariant and reconciliation suites in CI, plus scheduled production reconciliation and concurrency exercises for high risk money paths.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert immediately on out of balance conditions, duplicate economic effects, unexplained money creation or loss, settlement mismatch, reconciliation failure and unauthorized financial state change.
fields.Required observability: Track ledger invariants, balance deltas, transaction states, duplicate references, settlement status, reconciliation breaks, reversals, adjustments and financial control exceptions.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Financial invariants, atomicity, idempotency, precision, ordering, authorization, settlement or reconciliation controls are incomplete or inconsistent.
fields.Security consequences: Attackers may exploit the weakness for unauthorized financial gain, replay, limit bypass, account abuse or transaction manipulation.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt replay, double spend, limit bypass, account substitution, amount manipulation, race conditions and unauthorized financial transitions.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users may observe wrong balances, charges, credits, payouts, statements, limits, prices, settlement status or transaction history.

fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Safety requirements, hazard analysis, validation, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe behavior or human override controls are incomplete.

fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt unauthorized command, configuration change, identity substitution, telemetry spoofing and safety interlock bypass where cyber influence is possible.

fields.Business consequences: Potential safety incident, service suspension, recall, investigation, liability, regulatory action, operational interruption and loss of trust.
fields.Chaos or dependency failure test where r: Disconnect sensors, controllers, networks, power, cloud services or dependent systems as appropriate and verify safe degraded state, failover and operator visibility.
fields.Conditions required to trigger the probl: The software participates in Medical devices and digital health. A safety relevant sensor value, control command, clinical decision, physical process state or emergency workflow is processed incorrectly, late, out of sequence or without required validation.
fields.Data integrity consequences: Safety relevant records, measurements, commands or state may become incorrect, missing, duplicated, stale or wrongly associated.
fields.Detectability: Medium. Some failures are observable through alarms and telemetry, while silent sensor, state or decision corruption can remain difficult to detect.
fields.Detection strategy: Monitor safety relevant telemetry, command and sensor plausibility, missed deadlines, alarm integrity, configuration changes, control divergence and independent safety indicators.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, dependent on operational exposure, hardware conditions, integration complexity and control maturity
fields.Expected severity: Critical where the failure can affect human safety or hazardous physical processes, otherwise High
fields.Failure mechanism: The software produces, suppresses, delays or misroutes a safety relevant decision or control action, allowing physical or clinical state to diverge from safe limits.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Possible direct loss, remediation, recall, compensation, legal liability, regulatory penalties and operational recovery cost.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Where timing or concurrency matters, exercise peak event rates and worst case latency while asserting all safety deadlines and interlocks remain satisfied.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Move the affected function to a known safe state, stop unsafe automation, preserve telemetry, escalate to the responsible safety operator and isolate the faulty component or data source.
fields.Negative test: Inject impossible, stale, out of range, conflicting, missing and incorrectly associated safety relevant data and assert rejection, alarm or safe fallback.
fields.Owner: Clinical Informatics, Patient Safety and Health Platform Engineering
fields.Performance consequences: Latency, jitter or processing delay can itself violate safety timing requirements.
fields.Prevention strategy: Define safety requirements and hazard controls, validate sensor and control ranges, enforce safe state transitions, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe defaults, interlocks, human override and independently verified software where appropriate.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact may include exposure of patient, employee, location, operational or identity data where such data is processed.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Medical devices and digital health.
fields.Recovery strategy: Verify physical or clinical state, restore validated configuration or software, reconcile records, complete required safety review and only then return the system to normal operation.
fields.Regression protection: Run safety regression, simulation and fault injection for every relevant software, configuration, hardware and integration change.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Generate high priority alerts for safety limit violations, lost safety telemetry, interlock bypass, command disagreement, missed control deadline and unsafe state transition.
fields.Required observability: Track safety relevant sensor quality, control commands, interlock state, alarm state, timing deadlines, configuration version, fail safe activation and operator override.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Safety requirements, hazard analysis, validation, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe behavior or human override controls are incomplete.
fields.Security consequences: Security impact can become safety impact when an attacker can alter commands, measurements, identity, configuration or safety relevant data.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt unauthorized command, configuration change, identity substitution, telemetry spoofing and safety interlock bypass where cyber influence is possible.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users or operators may receive unsafe, delayed or incorrect guidance, controls, alerts or state information, with possible service interruption or physical consequences.

fields.Automated test: Create deterministic ledger or transaction tests for Exchange Gain Loss Error, including success, duplicate, retry, reversal, partial failure, ordering and reconciliation cases.
fields.Availability consequences: Correctness controls may require transaction suspension, degraded service or manual reconciliation, reducing availability.
fields.Blast radius: Single transaction, account, merchant, portfolio, tenant, settlement batch or the wider financial ledger
fields.Business consequences: Direct monetary loss, reconciliation breaks, customer disputes, fraud exposure, accounting misstatement, support load and regulatory or contractual consequences.
fields.Chaos or dependency failure test where r: Interrupt databases, payment providers, message delivery, settlement callbacks or workers between financial state transitions and verify atomicity, recoverability and reconciliation.
fields.Conditions required to trigger the probl: The software participates in Accounting, taxation, and ERP finance. A money changing, balance changing, settlement, reconciliation, pricing or financial state transition occurs under concurrency, retries, partial failure, timing boundaries or external integration delay.
fields.Data integrity consequences: Ledger, transaction, balance, settlement, accounting or reconciliation records may diverge or become duplicated, missing or inconsistent.
fields.Detectability: Medium. Reconciliation can expose many failures, but silent balance or posting drift may persist until downstream settlement or customer dispute.
fields.Detection strategy: Continuously reconcile balances, postings, settlement, external processor records and customer statements. Track duplicate references, invariant violations, unexplained adjustments and out of balance conditions.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium to High under real transaction volume unless financial invariants, idempotency and reconciliation are explicitly enforced
fields.Expected severity: High, and Critical where customer funds, settlement, regulated capital or material financial reporting are affected
fields.Failure mechanism: The authoritative financial state diverges from the intended economic event, causing an incorrect balance, posting, charge, payout, valuation, settlement or accounting result.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Direct financial loss, incorrect customer funds, chargebacks, restitution, reconciliation cost, penalties and incident cost are possible.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Run concurrent financial operations at realistic and peak volume, including retries and delayed callbacks, and prove balance, limit, ordering and idempotency invariants remain true.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Freeze or isolate the affected transaction path, prevent further financial mutation, preserve the event trail, calculate the authoritative state and route discrepancies to controlled reconciliation.
fields.Negative test: Test zero, negative, maximum, precision boundary, duplicate, stale, unauthorized, expired, reversed, out of order and conflicting financial operations relevant to the risk.
fields.Owner: Financial Systems Engineering and Risk Controls
fields.Performance consequences: Reconciliation, retry or repair work can increase database, queue and integration load.
fields.Prevention strategy: Model financial state with explicit immutable or auditable records, atomic transactions, idempotency, exact decimal arithmetic, ordering guarantees, authorization checks, limit enforcement and independent reconciliation.
fields.Privacy consequences: Financial records and identity data can create privacy impact if exposed or associated with the wrong user.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Accounting, taxation, and ERP finance.
fields.Recovery strategy: Reconstruct financial state from authoritative records, post controlled compensating entries where required, reconcile external systems and obtain financial control approval before resuming normal processing.
fields.Regression protection: Run financial invariant and reconciliation suites in CI, plus scheduled production reconciliation and concurrency exercises for high risk money paths.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert immediately on out of balance conditions, duplicate economic effects, unexplained money creation or loss, settlement mismatch, reconciliation failure and unauthorized financial state change.
fields.Required observability: Track ledger invariants, balance deltas, transaction states, duplicate references, settlement status, reconciliation breaks, reversals, adjustments and financial control exceptions.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Financial invariants, atomicity, idempotency, precision, ordering, authorization, settlement or reconciliation controls are incomplete or inconsistent.
fields.Security consequences: Attackers may exploit the weakness for unauthorized financial gain, replay, limit bypass, account abuse or transaction manipulation.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt replay, double spend, limit bypass, account substitution, amount manipulation, race conditions and unauthorized financial transitions.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users may observe wrong balances, charges, credits, payouts, statements, limits, prices, settlement status or transaction history.

fields.Automated test: Create deterministic simulation or hardware in the loop tests for Signalling Logic Error, including normal, boundary, invalid, stale, delayed and contradictory inputs.
fields.Availability consequences: Loss of availability can remove monitoring, control, treatment or emergency functions and may require a safe shutdown.
fields.Blast radius: Potentially affected person, device, vehicle, facility, operational site, customer population or public service
fields.Business consequences: Potential safety incident, service suspension, recall, investigation, liability, regulatory action, operational interruption and loss of trust.
fields.Chaos or dependency failure test where r: Disconnect sensors, controllers, networks, power, cloud services or dependent systems as appropriate and verify safe degraded state, failover and operator visibility.
fields.Conditions required to trigger the probl: The software participates in Rail and public transportation. A safety relevant sensor value, control command, clinical decision, physical process state or emergency workflow is processed incorrectly, late, out of sequence or without required validation.
fields.Data integrity consequences: Safety relevant records, measurements, commands or state may become incorrect, missing, duplicated, stale or wrongly associated.
fields.Detectability: Medium. Some failures are observable through alarms and telemetry, while silent sensor, state or decision corruption can remain difficult to detect.
fields.Detection strategy: Monitor safety relevant telemetry, command and sensor plausibility, missed deadlines, alarm integrity, configuration changes, control divergence and independent safety indicators.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, dependent on operational exposure, hardware conditions, integration complexity and control maturity
fields.Expected severity: Critical where the failure can affect human safety or hazardous physical processes, otherwise High
fields.Failure mechanism: The software produces, suppresses, delays or misroutes a safety relevant decision or control action, allowing physical or clinical state to diverge from safe limits.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Possible direct loss, remediation, recall, compensation, legal liability, regulatory penalties and operational recovery cost.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Where timing or concurrency matters, exercise peak event rates and worst case latency while asserting all safety deadlines and interlocks remain satisfied.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Move the affected function to a known safe state, stop unsafe automation, preserve telemetry, escalate to the responsible safety operator and isolate the faulty component or data source.
fields.Negative test: Inject impossible, stale, out of range, conflicting, missing and incorrectly associated safety relevant data and assert rejection, alarm or safe fallback.
fields.Performance consequences: Latency, jitter or processing delay can itself violate safety timing requirements.
fields.Prevention strategy: Define safety requirements and hazard controls, validate sensor and control ranges, enforce safe state transitions, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe defaults, interlocks, human override and independently verified software where appropriate.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact may include exposure of patient, employee, location, operational or identity data where such data is processed.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Rail and public transportation.
fields.Recovery strategy: Verify physical or clinical state, restore validated configuration or software, reconcile records, complete required safety review and only then return the system to normal operation.
fields.Regression protection: Run safety regression, simulation and fault injection for every relevant software, configuration, hardware and integration change.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Generate high priority alerts for safety limit violations, lost safety telemetry, interlock bypass, command disagreement, missed control deadline and unsafe state transition.
fields.Required observability: Track safety relevant sensor quality, control commands, interlock state, alarm state, timing deadlines, configuration version, fail safe activation and operator override.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Safety requirements, hazard analysis, validation, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe behavior or human override controls are incomplete.
fields.Security consequences: Security impact can become safety impact when an attacker can alter commands, measurements, identity, configuration or safety relevant data.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt unauthorized command, configuration change, identity substitution, telemetry spoofing and safety interlock bypass where cyber influence is possible.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users or operators may receive unsafe, delayed or incorrect guidance, controls, alerts or state information, with possible service interruption or physical consequences.

fields.Business consequences: Potential safety incident, service suspension, recall, investigation, liability, regulatory action, operational interruption and loss of trust.

fields.Conditions required to trigger the probl: The software participates in Real estate and property technology. A safety relevant sensor value, control command, clinical decision, physical process state or emergency workflow is processed incorrectly, late, out of sequence or without required validation.
fields.Data integrity consequences: Safety relevant records, measurements, commands or state may become incorrect, missing, duplicated, stale or wrongly associated.
fields.Detectability: Medium. Some failures are observable through alarms and telemetry, while silent sensor, state or decision corruption can remain difficult to detect.
fields.Detection strategy: Monitor safety relevant telemetry, command and sensor plausibility, missed deadlines, alarm integrity, configuration changes, control divergence and independent safety indicators.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, dependent on operational exposure, hardware conditions, integration complexity and control maturity
fields.Expected severity: Critical where the failure can affect human safety or hazardous physical processes, otherwise High
fields.Failure mechanism: The software produces, suppresses, delays or misroutes a safety relevant decision or control action, allowing physical or clinical state to diverge from safe limits.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Possible direct loss, remediation, recall, compensation, legal liability, regulatory penalties and operational recovery cost.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Where timing or concurrency matters, exercise peak event rates and worst case latency while asserting all safety deadlines and interlocks remain satisfied.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Move the affected function to a known safe state, stop unsafe automation, preserve telemetry, escalate to the responsible safety operator and isolate the faulty component or data source.
fields.Negative test: Inject impossible, stale, out of range, conflicting, missing and incorrectly associated safety relevant data and assert rejection, alarm or safe fallback.
fields.Performance consequences: Latency, jitter or processing delay can itself violate safety timing requirements.
fields.Prevention strategy: Define safety requirements and hazard controls, validate sensor and control ranges, enforce safe state transitions, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe defaults, interlocks, human override and independently verified software where appropriate.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact may include exposure of patient, employee, location, operational or identity data where such data is processed.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Real estate and property technology.
fields.Recovery strategy: Verify physical or clinical state, restore validated configuration or software, reconcile records, complete required safety review and only then return the system to normal operation.
fields.Regression protection: Run safety regression, simulation and fault injection for every relevant software, configuration, hardware and integration change.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Generate high priority alerts for safety limit violations, lost safety telemetry, interlock bypass, command disagreement, missed control deadline and unsafe state transition.
fields.Required observability: Track safety relevant sensor quality, control commands, interlock state, alarm state, timing deadlines, configuration version, fail safe activation and operator override.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Safety requirements, hazard analysis, validation, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe behavior or human override controls are incomplete.
fields.Security consequences: Security impact can become safety impact when an attacker can alter commands, measurements, identity, configuration or safety relevant data.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt unauthorized command, configuration change, identity substitution, telemetry spoofing and safety interlock bypass where cyber influence is possible.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users or operators may receive unsafe, delayed or incorrect guidance, controls, alerts or state information, with possible service interruption or physical consequences.

fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, rising with scale, complexity, age, dependency count and real world edge cases

fields.Required alert: Alert on invariant violation, repeated failed transition, unexplained state divergence, correctness breach, sustained error rate and security indicators.

fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.

fields.Privacy consequences: Financial records and identity data can create privacy impact if exposed or associated with the wrong user.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Government and public administration.
fields.Recovery strategy: Reconstruct financial state from authoritative records, post controlled compensating entries where required, reconcile external systems and obtain financial control approval before resuming normal processing.
fields.Regression protection: Run financial invariant and reconciliation suites in CI, plus scheduled production reconciliation and concurrency exercises for high risk money paths.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert immediately on out of balance conditions, duplicate economic effects, unexplained money creation or loss, settlement mismatch, reconciliation failure and unauthorized financial state change.
fields.Required observability: Track ledger invariants, balance deltas, transaction states, duplicate references, settlement status, reconciliation breaks, reversals, adjustments and financial control exceptions.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Financial invariants, atomicity, idempotency, precision, ordering, authorization, settlement or reconciliation controls are incomplete or inconsistent.
fields.Security consequences: Attackers may exploit the weakness for unauthorized financial gain, replay, limit bypass, account abuse or transaction manipulation.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt replay, double spend, limit bypass, account substitution, amount manipulation, race conditions and unauthorized financial transitions.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users may observe wrong balances, charges, credits, payouts, statements, limits, prices, settlement status or transaction history.

fields.Automated test: Create a deterministic security regression for Endpoint Agent Failure that reproduces the abuse or exploit condition and asserts denial, safe handling and complete audit evidence.
fields.Availability consequences: Attack activity or containment can reduce availability and may trigger cascading load or lockouts.
fields.Blast radius: User, tenant, dataset, privileged function, service, integration or entire platform depending on the trust boundary
fields.Business consequences: Fraud exposure, incident response cost, regulatory action, customer loss, service interruption and reputation damage are possible.
fields.Chaos or dependency failure test where r: Degrade identity, key management, policy, dependency or audit services where relevant and verify fail closed or explicitly approved degraded behavior.
fields.Conditions required to trigger the probl: The software participates in Cybersecurity products. Untrusted prompts, retrieved content, model output, tool results, changing model behavior or agent actions enter the AI execution path.
fields.Data integrity consequences: Protected data may be read, changed, deleted, forged, replayed or associated with the wrong identity.
fields.Detectability: Medium by default. High only after dedicated security telemetry, audit events, anomaly detection and deterministic abuse tests exist.
fields.Detection strategy: Correlate authentication, authorization denials, anomalous access, exploit signatures, sensitive operation audit events, integrity checks, abuse indicators and dependency scan findings.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, rising with internet exposure, privilege, attacker incentive, dependency count and control weakness
fields.Expected severity: High where exploitation crosses sensitive data or privileged operations, otherwise Medium
fields.Failure mechanism: The model or agent generates or acts on incorrect, malicious, stale or unauthorized information and propagates it into product state or external actions.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Fraud, investigation, remediation, legal, notification, recovery and infrastructure costs can increase.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Where abuse is volume sensitive, exercise the control at realistic and hostile concurrency and prove rate limits, lockout, isolation and resource protection do not create collateral denial of service.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Contain the affected identity, endpoint, tenant, dependency or trust boundary, revoke compromised credentials or sessions, disable the vulnerable path, block malicious traffic and preserve forensic evidence.
fields.Negative test: Supply malformed, boundary, unauthorized, cross user, cross tenant, replayed and privilege violating inputs relevant to the named risk and assert safe rejection.
fields.Performance consequences: Abuse traffic, scanning, brute force activity or exploit processing can increase resource consumption and latency.
fields.Prevention strategy: Apply deny by default authorization, least privilege, strong authentication, input validation, output encoding, parameterized operations, secret management, dependency controls, rate limits and abuse resistant workflow design as relevant to the named risk.
fields.Privacy consequences: Personal, tenant, credential or confidential data may be exposed, inferred, altered or exfiltrated.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Cybersecurity products.
fields.Recovery strategy: Patch or reconfigure the control, rotate affected secrets, reconcile unauthorized changes, restore clean state, verify through security tests and then reenable the path under heightened monitoring.
fields.Regression protection: Run deterministic security tests in CI, dependency and configuration scans on every release, and periodic adversarial testing for runtime only attack paths.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert on exploit indicators, authorization anomalies, credential attacks, privilege changes, sensitive data access anomalies, control disablement and repeated risk specific failures.
fields.Required observability: Track authentication, authorization decisions, denied operations, privileged actions, suspicious input, rate limits, session events, integrity changes and risk specific security counters.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Model inputs, retrieval, tool permissions, output validation, evaluation, grounding or human oversight are insufficient for nondeterministic AI behavior.
fields.Security consequences: Confidentiality, integrity or availability can be directly compromised across the affected trust boundary.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Use authenticated and unauthenticated abuse cases, cross user and cross tenant attempts, injection payloads, replay, enumeration and privilege escalation tests as relevant.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users may see unauthorized actions, account compromise, exposed information, blocked access, service degradation or fraudulent activity.

fields.Automated test: Create a deterministic automated regression that forces Duplicate Observation and asserts the expected state, denial, compensation, audit record and user outcome.
fields.Availability consequences: The failure can reduce availability directly or contribute to cascading failure when dependencies or shared resources are affected.
fields.Blast radius: Single record, workflow, tenant, dataset, batch, downstream system or entire source of truth
fields.Business consequences: Conversion loss, support load, SLA impact, operational interruption, contractual exposure, reputation damage or domain specific loss may result.
fields.Chaos or dependency failure test where r: Degrade, delay, disconnect, restart or partially fail relevant dependencies and verify the workflow remains recoverable and does not enter an invalid state.
fields.Conditions required to trigger the probl: The software participates in Scientific research and laboratory software. Data is created, updated, synchronized, migrated, replayed, reconciled or read across multiple components, versions or timing boundaries.
fields.Data integrity consequences: Data may become stale, duplicate, missing, inconsistent, wrongly associated or corrupted depending on the affected state transition.
fields.Detectability: Medium to Low because silent correctness drift can survive functional monitoring until reconciliation or audit.
fields.Detection strategy: Instrument the affected workflow and continuously check for the state contradiction, drift, duplication, omission or boundary violation represented by Duplicate Observation.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, rising with concurrency, integrations, migrations, retries, asynchronous processing and data age
fields.Expected severity: High when authoritative or regulated records are affected, otherwise Medium
fields.Failure mechanism: Different components or records disagree about the same real world fact, or data becomes stale, missing, duplicated, corrupted or wrongly associated.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Infrastructure, third party, support, remediation, fraud, compensation or recovery cost can increase.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Exercise the condition at realistic and beyond expected concurrency or data volume when scale or contention can affect correctness, and record the break point.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Contain the affected workflow, stop further propagation, preserve audit evidence, correct unsafe state and isolate dependent components until correctness is restored.
fields.Negative test: Supply malformed, boundary, duplicate, stale, unauthorized, contradictory and out of sequence conditions relevant to the risk and assert rejection or safe degradation.
fields.Owner: Quality Systems, Laboratory Informatics and GxP Engineering
fields.Performance consequences: The failure can increase latency, contention, retries, queueing, resource use or unnecessary work.
fields.Prevention strategy: Define the invariant represented by Duplicate Observation, encode it as an explicit state, validation, authorization, ordering, uniqueness, lifecycle or reconciliation rule, and prevent invalid transitions at every entry path.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact exists when personal, confidential, tenant scoped, location, health, financial or identity data is involved.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Scientific research and laboratory software.
fields.Recovery strategy: Restore a known good state, reconcile affected records and external systems, replay or compensate only through controlled idempotent procedures, then reenable traffic gradually.
fields.Regression protection: Run the deterministic test in CI where possible and schedule staging or production resilience exercises for runtime only conditions.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert on invariant violation, repeated failed transition, unexplained state divergence, correctness breach, sustained error rate and security indicators.
fields.Required observability: Track state transitions, invariant violations, errors, retries, queue depth, dependency health, reconciliation status and risk specific counters.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Data invariants, source of truth, versioning, validation, ordering, reconciliation or synchronization rules are incomplete.
fields.Security consequences: Security consequences arise if the failure crosses identity, trust, privilege, tenant or sensitive data boundaries.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt alternate path, cross user, cross tenant, replay, parameter manipulation and privilege boundary abuse where the risk can be attacker influenced.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users may observe the direct manifestation of Duplicate Observation, including incorrect state, delayed processing, duplicate actions, missing results, inaccessible functionality or misleading information.

fields.Prevention strategy: Define the invariant represented by Contribution Limit Enforcement Failure, encode it as an explicit state, validation, authorization, ordering, uniqueness, lifecycle or reconciliation rule, and prevent invalid transitions at every entry path.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact exists when personal, confidential, tenant scoped, location, health, financial or identity data is involved.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Pensions and retirement systems.
fields.Recovery strategy: Restore a known good state, reconcile affected records and external systems, replay or compensate only through controlled idempotent procedures, then reenable traffic gradually.
fields.Regression protection: Run the deterministic test in CI where possible and schedule staging or production resilience exercises for runtime only conditions.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert on invariant violation, repeated failed transition, unexplained state divergence, correctness breach, sustained error rate and security indicators.
fields.Required observability: Track state transitions, invariant violations, errors, retries, queue depth, dependency health, reconciliation status and risk specific counters.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: The relevant domain invariant, boundary condition, lifecycle rule or operational constraint is not explicitly encoded, validated and tested.
fields.Security consequences: Security consequences arise if the failure crosses identity, trust, privilege, tenant or sensitive data boundaries.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt alternate path, cross user, cross tenant, replay, parameter manipulation and privilege boundary abuse where the risk can be attacker influenced.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users may observe the direct manifestation of Contribution Limit Enforcement Failure, including incorrect state, delayed processing, duplicate actions, missing results, inaccessible functionality or misleading information.

fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.

fields.Business consequences: Potential safety incident, service suspension, recall, investigation, liability, regulatory action, operational interruption and loss of trust.
fields.Chaos or dependency failure test where r: Disconnect sensors, controllers, networks, power, cloud services or dependent systems as appropriate and verify safe degraded state, failover and operator visibility.
fields.Conditions required to trigger the probl: The software participates in Robotics and autonomous systems. A safety relevant sensor value, control command, clinical decision, physical process state or emergency workflow is processed incorrectly, late, out of sequence or without required validation.
fields.Data integrity consequences: Safety relevant records, measurements, commands or state may become incorrect, missing, duplicated, stale or wrongly associated.
fields.Detectability: Medium. Some failures are observable through alarms and telemetry, while silent sensor, state or decision corruption can remain difficult to detect.
fields.Detection strategy: Monitor safety relevant telemetry, command and sensor plausibility, missed deadlines, alarm integrity, configuration changes, control divergence and independent safety indicators.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, dependent on operational exposure, hardware conditions, integration complexity and control maturity
fields.Expected severity: Critical where the failure can affect human safety or hazardous physical processes, otherwise High
fields.Failure mechanism: The software produces, suppresses, delays or misroutes a safety relevant decision or control action, allowing physical or clinical state to diverge from safe limits.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Possible direct loss, remediation, recall, compensation, legal liability, regulatory penalties and operational recovery cost.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Where timing or concurrency matters, exercise peak event rates and worst case latency while asserting all safety deadlines and interlocks remain satisfied.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Move the affected function to a known safe state, stop unsafe automation, preserve telemetry, escalate to the responsible safety operator and isolate the faulty component or data source.
fields.Negative test: Inject impossible, stale, out of range, conflicting, missing and incorrectly associated safety relevant data and assert rejection, alarm or safe fallback.
fields.Performance consequences: Latency, jitter or processing delay can itself violate safety timing requirements.
fields.Prevention strategy: Define safety requirements and hazard controls, validate sensor and control ranges, enforce safe state transitions, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe defaults, interlocks, human override and independently verified software where appropriate.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact may include exposure of patient, employee, location, operational or identity data where such data is processed.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Robotics and autonomous systems.
fields.Recovery strategy: Verify physical or clinical state, restore validated configuration or software, reconcile records, complete required safety review and only then return the system to normal operation.
fields.Regression protection: Run safety regression, simulation and fault injection for every relevant software, configuration, hardware and integration change.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Generate high priority alerts for safety limit violations, lost safety telemetry, interlock bypass, command disagreement, missed control deadline and unsafe state transition.
fields.Required observability: Track safety relevant sensor quality, control commands, interlock state, alarm state, timing deadlines, configuration version, fail safe activation and operator override.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Safety requirements, hazard analysis, validation, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe behavior or human override controls are incomplete.
fields.Security consequences: Security impact can become safety impact when an attacker can alter commands, measurements, identity, configuration or safety relevant data.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt unauthorized command, configuration change, identity substitution, telemetry spoofing and safety interlock bypass where cyber influence is possible.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users or operators may receive unsafe, delayed or incorrect guidance, controls, alerts or state information, with possible service interruption or physical consequences.

fields.Data integrity consequences: Safety relevant records, measurements, commands or state may become incorrect, missing, duplicated, stale or wrongly associated.
fields.Detectability: Medium. Some failures are observable through alarms and telemetry, while silent sensor, state or decision corruption can remain difficult to detect.

fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, dependent on operational exposure, hardware conditions, integration complexity and control maturity
fields.Expected severity: Critical where the failure can affect human safety or hazardous physical processes, otherwise High
fields.Failure mechanism: The software produces, suppresses, delays or misroutes a safety relevant decision or control action, allowing physical or clinical state to diverge from safe limits.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Possible direct loss, remediation, recall, compensation, legal liability, regulatory penalties and operational recovery cost.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Where timing or concurrency matters, exercise peak event rates and worst case latency while asserting all safety deadlines and interlocks remain satisfied.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Move the affected function to a known safe state, stop unsafe automation, preserve telemetry, escalate to the responsible safety operator and isolate the faulty component or data source.
fields.Negative test: Inject impossible, stale, out of range, conflicting, missing and incorrectly associated safety relevant data and assert rejection, alarm or safe fallback.
fields.Performance consequences: Latency, jitter or processing delay can itself violate safety timing requirements.
fields.Prevention strategy: Define safety requirements and hazard controls, validate sensor and control ranges, enforce safe state transitions, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe defaults, interlocks, human override and independently verified software where appropriate.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact may include exposure of patient, employee, location, operational or identity data where such data is processed.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk arises from whether the software correctly represents the real world state, calculations, workflows and invariants of Robotics and autonomous systems.
fields.Recovery strategy: Verify physical or clinical state, restore validated configuration or software, reconcile records, complete required safety review and only then return the system to normal operation.
fields.Regression protection: Run safety regression, simulation and fault injection for every relevant software, configuration, hardware and integration change.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Generate high priority alerts for safety limit violations, lost safety telemetry, interlock bypass, command disagreement, missed control deadline and unsafe state transition.
fields.Required observability: Track safety relevant sensor quality, control commands, interlock state, alarm state, timing deadlines, configuration version, fail safe activation and operator override.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Safety requirements, hazard analysis, validation, redundancy, timing constraints, fail safe behavior or human override controls are incomplete.
fields.Security consequences: Security impact can become safety impact when an attacker can alter commands, measurements, identity, configuration or safety relevant data.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt unauthorized command, configuration change, identity substitution, telemetry spoofing and safety interlock bypass where cyber influence is possible.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users or operators may receive unsafe, delayed or incorrect guidance, controls, alerts or state information, with possible service interruption or physical consequences.

fields.Architecture or component affected: product state machine, ledger or financial records, transaction engine, API, persistence, reconciliation, integrations, audit and user interface
fields.Automated test: Create deterministic ledger or transaction tests for Chargeback Lifecycle Corruption, including success, duplicate, retry, reversal, partial failure, ordering and reconciliation cases.
fields.Availability consequences: Loss of availability can remove monitoring, control, treatment or emergency functions and may require a safe shutdown.
fields.Blast radius: Potentially affected person, device, vehicle, facility, operational site, customer population or public service
fields.Business consequences: Potential safety incident, service suspension, recall, investigation, liability, regulatory action, operational interruption and loss of trust.
fields.Chaos or dependency failure test where r: Interrupt databases, payment providers, message delivery, settlement callbacks or workers between financial state transitions and verify atomicity, recoverability and reconciliation.
fields.Conditions required to trigger the probl: The product implements Card issuing platform. A money changing, balance changing, settlement, reconciliation, pricing or financial state transition occurs under concurrency, retries, partial failure, timing boundaries or external integration delay.
fields.Data integrity consequences: Safety relevant records, measurements, commands or state may become incorrect, missing, duplicated, stale or wrongly associated.
fields.Detectability: Medium. Some failures are observable through alarms and telemetry, while silent sensor, state or decision corruption can remain difficult to detect.
fields.Detection strategy: Continuously reconcile balances, postings, settlement, external processor records and customer statements. Track duplicate references, invariant violations, unexplained adjustments and out of balance conditions.
fields.Existing protections: No implementation specific protection was evidenced in the supplied material.
fields.Expected likelihood: Medium, dependent on operational exposure, hardware conditions, integration complexity and control maturity
fields.Expected severity: Critical where the failure can affect human safety or hazardous physical processes, otherwise High
fields.Failure mechanism: The authoritative financial state diverges from the intended economic event, causing an incorrect balance, posting, charge, payout, valuation, settlement or accounting result.
fields.Final status: FAIL. No implementation specific acceptance evidence supplied.
fields.Financial consequences: Possible direct loss, remediation, recall, compensation, legal liability, regulatory penalties and operational recovery cost.
fields.Known aliases: No separate alias required for this catalogue entry
fields.Load or concurrency test where relevant: Run concurrent financial operations at realistic and peak volume, including retries and delayed callbacks, and prove balance, limit, ordering and idempotency invariants remain true.
fields.Mitigation strategy: Freeze or isolate the affected transaction path, prevent further financial mutation, preserve the event trail, calculate the authoritative state and route discrepancies to controlled reconciliation.
fields.Negative test: Test zero, negative, maximum, precision boundary, duplicate, stale, unauthorized, expired, reversed, out of order and conflicting financial operations relevant to the risk.
fields.Owner: Product Engineering, Financial Controls and Risk Engineering
fields.Performance consequences: Latency, jitter or processing delay can itself violate safety timing requirements.
fields.Prevention strategy: Model financial state with explicit immutable or auditable records, atomic transactions, idempotency, exact decimal arithmetic, ordering guarantees, authorization checks, limit enforcement and independent reconciliation.
fields.Privacy consequences: Privacy impact may include exposure of patient, employee, location, operational or identity data where such data is processed.
fields.Protection weaknesses: Production acceptance evidence is absent. The risk must remain open until the control is implemented and tested.
fields.Reason for applicability: The risk is created by the particular state machine, actors, money flows, entitlements, data and user journeys of a Card issuing platform.
fields.Recovery strategy: Reconstruct financial state from authoritative records, post controlled compensating entries where required, reconcile external systems and obtain financial control approval before resuming normal processing.
fields.Regression protection: Run financial invariant and reconciliation suites in CI, plus scheduled production reconciliation and concurrency exercises for high risk money paths.
fields.Required acceptance evidence: Automated test output, load or chaos results where relevant, logs or traces, configuration proof, domain or regulatory evidence, dashboards, runbook and remediation record.
fields.Required alert: Alert immediately on out of balance conditions, duplicate economic effects, unexplained money creation or loss, settlement mismatch, reconciliation failure and unauthorized financial state change.
fields.Required observability: Track ledger invariants, balance deltas, transaction states, duplicate references, settlement status, reconciliation breaks, reversals, adjustments and financial control exceptions.
fields.Residual risk after mitigation: Residual risk must be explicitly accepted only after the required controls and tests pass, measured operating limits are known, and accountable owners approve the remaining exposure.
fields.Root cause: Financial invariants, atomicity, idempotency, precision, ordering, authorization, settlement or reconciliation controls are incomplete or inconsistent.
fields.Security consequences: Security impact can become safety impact when an attacker can alter commands, measurements, identity, configuration or safety relevant data.
fields.Security or abuse test where relevant: Attempt replay, double spend, limit bypass, account substitution, amount manipulation, race conditions and unauthorized financial transitions.
fields.User visible symptoms: Users or operators may receive unsafe, delayed or incorrect guidance, controls, alerts or state information, with possible service interruption or physical consequences.
